description: Mixture of Experts (Qwen4ExpTextSparseMoeBlock) layer-0 mlp reference fixture. Router weight VALUES are the real, complete Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model.language_model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight tensor (all 512 real experts -- num_experts is the axis this mechanism exists to test, kept unsliced, docs/GATED_RESIDUAL.md's HC_COUNT precedent), sliced from hidden_size=2560 down to 16 (first 16 input columns kept). The router's REAL top-10 selection on this sliced router + a real hand-picked input names which 10 of the 512 experts are actually consulted; TWO more real, different experts ('decoys') were also fetched for the presence/mutation reference. Only those 12 experts' real model.language_model.layers.0.mlp.experts.{gate_up_proj,down_proj} slabs were extracted (never the full 512-expert, multi-GB tensors) via HTTP Range requests against the real safetensors shards, sliced from moe_intermediate_size=640 down to 8. The shared expert's real gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj/shared_expert_gate weights were fetched in full (small enough) and sliced the same way. The forward pass itself is the real transformers==5.16.1 Qwen4ExpTextSparseMoeBlock.forward() (dispatched to its eager reference implementation via config._experts_implementation='eager'), run on CPU with these real, sliced weight values -- nothing about this fixture is a hand re-derivation of the formula.
dtype: float32 little-endian, raw flat binary, row-major (C order)
weight_convention: raw PyTorch nn.Linear [out_features, in_features] convention, UNTRANSPOSED -- the test file transposes into this project's own [rows=in, cols=out] convention before calling sub0::moe::*, matching gdn_math.hpp's/gated_residual_math.hpp's own fixture-test precedent.
mutant_construction: the real router's OWN top-10 selection with its FIRST TWO slots forcibly replaced by the two decoy experts (same routing WEIGHTS, different experts consulted) -- output_mutant is the real Qwen4ExpTextExperts.forward() + real shared-expert path re-run with that forced selection, on the SAME input and SAME weights otherwise. max|output_mutant - output| is real and nonzero (see the final report for the exact number) -- proves the reference output genuinely depends on WHICH experts are consulted, not just that a plausible output comes out.
notes: hidden_size (2560->16) and d_ff (640->8) are ordinary Linear-projection widths, freely sliced (first N columns/rows kept, matching every prior fixture in this thread's own slicing convention); num_experts (512) and num_experts_per_tok (10) are BOTH kept at their real values -- the routing/selection behavior this whole mechanism exists to test would degenerate at a small num_experts (e.g. top-2-of-4 barely exercises 'select some, ignore most').

The module's own top-10 selection on the sliced router was independently re-derived in plain numpy (softmax + argsort) BEFORE any expert weight was fetched, to decide which few of the 512 experts were worth downloading -- then cross-checked EXACTLY against the real module's own torch.topk output once it ran (see the final report); the two agreed, confirming this fixture's own expert selection is genuinely the real router's, not a hand guess.
